newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major condemns fellow Conservative for slurs.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major condemns fellow Conservative for slurs.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major condemned on Wednesday an outspoken member of his Conservative party who caused a storm by heaping personal abuse on political friend and foe alike.

David Evans, a colourful right-winger, said the female candidate of the main opposition Labour party who is trying to unseat him at the coming general election had "never done a proper job" and was the mother of "three bastard children".

In an interview at a local school that he thought was confidential, Evans went on to describe Prime Minister John Major as "vindictive and not forgiving" and used the phrase "black bastard" when discussing crime.
He also described cabinet minister Virginia Bottomley as "dead from the neck upwards". The transcript of his interview was given to a regional television station.
Asked at a news conference whether he condemned Evans's remarks, Major said without hesitation, "Yes".
Although Evans is not influential within the ruling party, his outburst ensured the already politically beleaguered Major another day of negative headlines in Britain's daily newspapers.
"Big mouth puts his foot in it," the pro-Conservative Daily Mail said of Evans on its front page.
Evans, a self-made millionaire, issued a grudging apology, saying the comments had been taken out of context.

"After due consideration, I regret some of the things I said and I apologise to the prime minister and to others for any embarrassment or offence which may have been caused," he said in a statement issued by the Conservative party.
Bottomley, the national heritage secretary, tried to make light of the row. "I have had a very gallant and elegant apology from him, which is much appreciated," she told BBC radio.
Evans's Labour opponent at the coming election, Melanie Johnson, said she was appalled by his outburst.

"I don't think these kind of comments go down well," said Johnson, a full-time schools inspector and magistrate who has three children by the man with whom she has lived for 18 years. "I think it does show he must be pretty desperate."
